sources.citation: B. F. Skinner (1948). 'Superstition' in the pigeon. Journal of Experimental Psychology.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1948) in Journal of Experimental Psychology establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: J. E. Staddon, Virginia L. Simmelhag (1971). The "supersitition" experiment: A reexamination of its implications for the principles of adaptive behavior. Psychological Review.
sources.notes: Staddon & Simmelhag's landmark replication reinterpreting Skinner's pigeon 'superstitions' into interim and terminal responses.

sources.citation: J. E. R. Staddon, D. T. Cerutti (2003). Operant Conditioning. Annual Review of Psychology.
sources.notes: Comprehensive theoretical and neurobehavioral review of operant reinforcement schedules and response selection.

sources.citation: Muhammad Lukman Arif, Nurul Atik Hamida, Wahidah Ma’rifatunnisa’, Nurhasanah Nurhasanah (2026). Implementasi Teori Operant Conditioning B. F Skinner dalam Pembentukan Kedisiplinan Shalat Berjamaah pada Peserta Didik Usia Remaja. Konstruktivisme : Jurnal Pendidikan dan Pembelajaran.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2026) in Konstruktivisme : Jurnal Pendidikan dan Pembelajaran extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Koichi Ono (1987). SUPERSTITIOUS BEHAVIOR IN HUMANS. Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior.
sources.notes: Experimental replication of non-contingent fixed-time reinforcement schedules generating superstitious lever rituals in human participants.

sources.citation: Thomas M. Leeder (2022). Behaviorism, Skinner, and Operant Conditioning: Considerations for Sport Coaching Practice. Strategies.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2022) in Strategies extending the foundational findings.
